nodes.description: Stored bytes32 hash used as the secret-key gate for withdraw; initially zero and set once by setup or new_hash.
Address of the contract deployer; controls extract() and receives the selfdestruct balance.
Constructor that assigns msg.sender to owner at deployment time.
Payable function that checks msg.sender == tx.origin and the keccak256 key against keyHash, then transfers the whole balance to msg.sender when msg.value > 0.5 ether.
Public function that sets keyHash from keccak256(key) only while keyHash is still zero.
Public function that sets keyHash to a caller-supplied bytes32 only while keyHash is still zero.
Owner-only function that calls selfdestruct(owner), destroying the contract and sending the balance to owner.
View function returning the current owner address.
Payable fallback function that accepts ether, funding the balance that withdraw can drain.
Caller-controlled address used for ownership assignment, the tx.origin check and the destination of the balance transfer.
Transaction origin used as an authorization condition, enabling phishing-style bypass of the withdraw gate.
msg.sender.transfer(address(this).balance) forwards the entire contract balance to an unauthenticated external address before any state change.
selfdestruct(owner) permanently destroys the contract and forwards its balance to owner.
Caller-supplied string key whose keccak256 hash must match keyHash to pass the withdraw gate.
Caller-supplied string key hashed and stored into keyHash by setup.
Caller-supplied bytes32 value stored directly into keyHash by new_hash.

edges.reason: msg.sender is written into the owner state variable during construction, establishing the privileged account.
The require(msg.sender == tx.origin) check gates withdraw using an attacker-influenceable caller identity.
tx.origin is read as the authorization condition in withdraw, allowing phishing contracts to pass the check on behalf of a victim.
keyHash is compared against keccak256(abi.encodePacked(key)) to decide whether the withdrawal proceeds.
The key parameter is hashed and compared with keyHash to control the withdraw branch.
A caller-supplied key alone determines whether the full contract balance is transferred out.
withdraw executes the balance transfer directly with no state update or reentrancy guard.
The external transfer to msg.sender can call back into the payable withdraw/fallback before balances settle.
Ether accepted by the payable fallback accumulates as the contract balance that the transfer operation drains.
extract requires msg.sender == owner before executing the destructive selfdestruct.
The owner state variable is the beneficiary of selfdestruct and the account authorized to trigger it.
The setup key parameter is hashed and written into keyHash, defining the withdrawal secret.
setup stores keccak256(key) into the keyHash state variable when it is still zero.
The _keyHash parameter is written into keyHash by new_hash, letting the deployer choose the secret directly.
new_hash assigns the caller-supplied bytes32 to the keyHash state variable.
new_hash can only initialize keyHash while it is zero, so whoever calls it first fixes the withdrawal secret.
get_owner returns the owner state variable to any caller.

normalization_plan.reason: The withdraw key parameter is only used inside withdraw's hash comparison that authorizes the balance drain, so it collapses into the withdraw function node.
The setup key parameter exists solely to compute keyHash inside setup, so it is absorbed into the setup function node.
The new_hash _keyHash parameter exists solely to assign keyHash inside new_hash, so it is absorbed into the new_hash function node.
